What it means: Chair Weber [11:39] convened a Boston City Council Committee on Ways and Means hearing [11:42] regarding Dockets 1671 and 1673 [13:15, 15:09]. These orders transfer funds from collective bargaining reserves [15:14, 16:26] to cover FY27 cost items [13:21, 15:24], including a 2% wage increase [14:33, 16:08] totaling $1,951,894 for the Patrolmen's Benevolent Society [13:37, 13:50] and $1,366,093 for the Superior Officers and Detectives units [15:20, 15:34, 15:58]. Budget Director Jim Williamson [22:05, 22:09] explained that the transfers shift reserve allocations into the active departmental budget [23:18, 23:25] to account for approved contract terms [23:03, 24:27].

Who moved it: Chair Weber opened and led the hearing [11:39, 12:14], joined by Councilors Flynn [17:11], Murphy [34:48], and Fitzgerald [40:43]. City Budget Director Jim Williamson presented the budget details [22:05, 22:14], and Bob Griffin provided testimony on behalf of the detectives union [47:02, 47:38]. Although the transcript states that the matters were sponsored and referred to the committee [16:41, 16:44], the snippet does not explicitly list the sponsor's name [16:41].

What to watch: Chair Weber noted that the dockets could be brought up for a city council vote on Wednesday [1:06:08]. During the meeting, councilors raised questions regarding detective staffing shortages [36:22, 42:11], officers working 16-hour shifts [25:31, 28:44], and health screenings funded directly by the union [50:21, 53:51]. Councilor Flynn recalled previous budget amendment proposals for police wellness [1:06:33, 1:07:08], while Chair Weber recommended building consensus among councilors for future budget actions [1:07:56, 1:08:35]. The transcript does not show a vote being taken before the meeting adjourned [1:08:55].

summary: During the September 20, 2026 hearing [11:45], the Boston City Council Committee on Ways and Means [11:42] discussed Docket 1671 [13:15] and Docket 1673 [15:09] concerning fiscal year 2027 appropriations to fund collective bargaining wage increases for the Boston Police Detectives Benevolent Society [13:32] and the Boston Police Superior Officers Unit [15:30]. Budget Director Jim Williamson detailed how the orders move funds from reserve accounts into the department budget to cover a two percent pay increase and other established contract provisions [22:05], [23:18], [32:43]. Councilors and union representative Bob Griffin [47:02] also addressed detective staffing shortages [36:22], [41:38], [47:38], heavy case loads [48:54], and union-funded health and cancer wellness screenings [28:57], [49:50], [53:35]. No votes were taken during the meeting before Chair Weber adjourned the hearing [1:08:58].
